title: IS12:: calculating1.c (2.3)

lines.explanation: The result of this integer addition operation will occupy exactly 5 positions in the output. Since there are only 4 digits in the result, one position will be left blank. To use leading zero instead of leading blank use %05d istead of %5d
The  result of this floating point multiplication will occupy exactly 7 positions of the output, out of them exactly 1 after decimal pount. This is prescribed by %7.1f specification

This line will print 5 / 2 = 2 because of integer division. The results of dividing an integer into another integer has to be also integer, so only an integer part will be returned as result. (the correct math result is 2.5, but C is not math!)

A way to fight integer division if you need a real result. This line will print 2.5 in a standard floating point format. Since 5.0 is a floating point number, 2 will be also converted from integer to floating point and 5.0/2.0 will result in 2.5
This line will print 1 - the remainder of integer division (5 / 2). The remainder operation % has to be applied to integer numbers and its result is integer.
